description: Fan-out vs. serial convergence gate for swarm-agent-pattern's SwarmRuntime. Each case is one scenario from that repo's scripts/benchmark_fanout_vs_serial.py, run for real through SwarmRuntime (fan-out, all agents propose every round) and a serial baseline built from the same SwarmAgent/Blackboard/Proposal classes (one agent proposes per round, cycling the roster), under two round-budget conditions ('matched' = same max_rounds as fanout, 'extended' = max_rounds * roster size). Agents (ExplorationAgent/RiskAgent/SynthesisAgent) are deterministic stubs -- no LLM calls, no API key, no randomness. Uses the registry's existing router_invariant scorer ('equals') rather than a new scorer kind, since router_invariant's generic equals contract already fits exact-match deterministic checks. See swarm-agent-pattern/docs/receipts/benchmark.md for full methodology and the honest reading of results (fan-out wins on rounds-to-convergence under a matched round budget; serial catches up to the same convergence_target when given an equal total invocation budget; 2 of 9 scenarios are deliberately structurally unreachable for both conditions).
